profile.campus: Cheyenne, Laramie County, Wyoming (Microsoft Azure data center operations since 2012)
profile.address: North Range Business Park Trail System, Laramie County, Wyoming, 82005
profile.reading:
This building is part of Microsoft's Cheyenne, Laramie County, Wyoming data center operations, where Microsoft has operated since 2012 and now employs approximately 320 full-time staff. Microsoft's own newsroom announced in April 2026 its intent to purchase roughly 3,200 acres across two parcels south and near Cheyenne for major new data center development, 200 acres in Bison Business Park and about 3,000 acres in Southeast Cheyenne, which local and trade press including Cowboy State Daily described as roughly tripling Microsoft's existing Cheyenne footprint; Microsoft said the expansion would follow a multiyear planning and development process including public hearings and community engagement before construction begins. In 2025, Microsoft's existing Cheyenne facilities generated more than $11 million in local property taxes, making the company Cheyenne's top taxpayer and Laramie County's second-largest. Microsoft has committed more than $68 million in completed and planned local infrastructure improvements, including roadway upgrades, water infrastructure, and storm sewer enhancements, and has donated $4.7 million across 56 community projects since 2018. The company's Datacenter Academy at Laramie County Community College has trained more than 1,000 students since 2019 for data center careers. Microsoft has pledged to offset the expansion's electricity consumption with carbon-free energy and to replenish more water than its Cheyenne operations consume through partnerships with local conservation organizations. Microsoft has not published this specific building's individual square footage or MW capacity, consistent with its general practice of not disclosing per-building specifics for its Azure data centers.

Cheyenne Light, Fuel and Power, the local utility, and the Wyoming Public Service Commission have both been named in local coverage of Microsoft's proposed 3,200-acre expansion as parties the company will need to work with on power delivery for the new campus, and Wyoming state officials have highlighted the project as part of the state's broader push to diversify its historically energy-and-minerals-dependent economy toward data infrastructure.

reading.body:
Microsoft does not publish power capacity, square footage, or facility-specific details for individual Azure data center campuses, including this Cheyenne-area site. The operator discloses only aggregate worldwide statistics: 40+ gigawatts of renewable energy contracted globally across 500+ data centers in 80+ regions. Wyoming has four mapped data center facilities but none with published megawatt figures, making this campus impossible to size against regional peers or to rank within the state by disclosed capacity.

Microsoft announced expansion intent for Cheyenne and pursued acquisition of approximately 3,200 acres south of the city, suggesting material growth plans, but the scale of this campus relative to that land position is not disclosed. Without published power consumption or floor area, the campus cannot be assessed for how much GPU density or training workload it qualifies to absorb.

The absence of published specifications is Microsoft's documented policy across its data center portfolio and reflects no gap in reporting for this site alone. For readers tracking AI infrastructure constraints by state and by facility, Wyoming and this campus remain unquantified in the published record.
